Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. The players and the umpires return for the second essay. Johnson Charles and Jewel Andrew are to open the batting for the West Indies. It will be Shaheen Afridi with the ball for Pakistan. Here we go!
...THE CHASE...

If West Indies lose this game, they have to blame the fielding department. They were very loose on the field, dropping a couple of sitters and occasionally being cosy while chasing the ball. The bowlers executed the plans and put in a lot of effort to keep Pakistan under pressure but every time it was released by a mistake on the field. Shamar Joseph was the pick of the bowlers for his three wickets. One surprising act from West Indies was that they didn't use Gudakesh Motie. The reason is unknown. Can West Indies chase it down and start the series on a positive note? Time will tell. Stay tuned for the chase.

Shamar Joseph is up for a chat. He says that the wicket was on the slower side, and hitting the right areas and keeping it on the stumps was the key. Shares that executing the plans is important, and it worked well for him. Mentions that the coaches reached out to him to join the squad late, and he was up for the challenge. Closes by adding that they need to get a good start with the bat and keep the momentum.

It wasn't a smooth ride for Pakistan as they lost wickets at regular intervals, it was at crucial stages when they were trying to up the ante. Everyone contributed to the overall total. The core partnership came in between Fakhar Zaman and Saim Ayub in the start of the innings when Pakistan were trying to lay a nice foundation for others to finish it off. Fakhar Zaman tried a bit too hard to change gears but struggled throughout his innings. His struggle meant Saim Ayub had to take the role and he delivered with a fine fifty to his name. Pakistan might have scored 10-15 more but they'll be confident going into the chase.

Pakistan have ended the innings well and the little cameos from their middle-order could make a massive difference later in the game. This is a formidable total. Just above average on this ground and Pakistan will be happy with the effort they have put in.

The players from both teams walk out for the national anthems. It will be Pakistan's first, followed by the West Indies' national anthem.

Salman Agha, the captain of Pakistan says the preparations have been outstanding and the players are ready and excited for the series. Shares it's a good opportunity to lead this team, they have a balanced squad which makes his job easier. Reckons they need to follow the process and believe they can beat any team in the world.

Shai Hope, the skipper of West Indies says they will bowl first as batting second is easier on this ground. Tells it's a quick turnaround for them from the past series, they didn't get much time to think but hopes to do well in the middle phase. Informs they are playing three spinners and four seamers.

TOSS - West Indies have won the toss and will BOWL.

West Indies have been under rebuild for ages and there’s no shy in saying they have struggled every moment. The talent they possess is one of the best in the world but as a team, they barely put in a performance. To recollect the memories, West Indies recently lost against Australia 8-0. Yes, that included five T20Is. West Indies have retained most of the squad, with the only big name missing being Andre Russell, who retired from this format. The sun rises again for West Indies to get together and perform. Against them is a team who are in a similar situation but still better and favourites to win the series. A big series for both the teams. Who do you think will win? Toss and team sheets next.

Pakistan and the West Indies, two giants of this format, have struggled badly lately and are in a phase they haven’t experienced before. Pakistan recently lost to their continental rivals, Bangladesh, 1-2, with their batting department under scrutiny. They were bowled out twice inside 20 overs which you rarely see with this team. Overall, it was a surprising series for most of the cricketing nerds as Pakistan were expected to win but in the rebuilding phase, they got hammered.

Hello everyone to the first of the three T20Is between West Indies and Pakistan. The shortest format is taking place in Lauderhill, Florida and will be followed by a 3-match ODI series held in Trinidad.
...MATCH DAY...

Fireworks are expected in Florida as West Indies and Pakistan kick off their three-match T20I series, with both teams desperate to bounce back - West Indies reeling from a 5-0 drubbing by Australia and Pakistan coming off a shock series defeat to Bangladesh. For the Windies, skipper Shai Hope’s composure and the power-hitting trio of Brandon King, Shimron Hetmyer, and Sherfane Rutherford will be key to posting big totals, while Akeal Hosein and Alzarri Joseph lead a bowling attack that must step up after a poor run. The all round abilities of Romario Shepherd and Jason Holder will be crucial as well. Pakistan, missing Babar Azam, will look to Fakhar Zaman’s aggression, Saim Ayub’s flair, and Khushdil Shah’s finishing power, with Shaheen Afridi and Haris Rauf spearheading a potent pace unit backed by Abrar Ahmed’s spin. The likes of Salman Agha and Mohammad Haris only adds further depth and quality to the side. The Caribbean side’s strength lies in explosive batting and familiarity with Florida’s conditions, though their bowling remains suspect, while Pakistan boast a lethal new-ball attack but face questions over middle-order consistency. With both sides desperate to reset after recent setbacks, expect a fiercely contested, high-energy opener to ignite the series.
